It does not consider people’s needs, aspirations, barriers or extra costs—it is just about what someone cannot do. Many find it adversarial and dehumanising. It struggles to reflect fluctuating and cumulative conditions properly, and it too often leaves people fearing that work, treatment or greater independence will count against them. Far from supporting independence, it can be a barrier to it.
